chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked about Mut'ah, and he said:

"Indeed, Mut'ah today is not as it was before today. For at that time, they [the women] were believed [regarding their lineage and waiting period], but today they are not believed, so ask about them."
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in the ruling of Mut'ah today compared to the past according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the legal status of Mut'ah has evolved, noting that women in temporary marriage were previously considered 'believed' (mu'manat) with recognized lineage, whereas in the contemporary era, their status requires specific verification. This distinction highlights the dynamic nature of fiqh in Shia tradition, where the application of a ruling may depend on the social and religious context of the participants. The narration underscores the importance of investigating the religious adherence of the woman to determine the validity of the contract's conditions.
